title: People & Roster
objective: Every human the Oxford Lancers hold is findable, readable, correctable and de-duplicable by the four-role group, and this season's squad is a working command surface rather than a four-column list. An operator can find any person by name or alias; open a record that states what is known, what is not recorded, and who supplied each value; correct any of it with the change attributed and the old value superseded rather than erased; add a coach or committee member who holds no membership; merge two records for the same human without losing either identity; work a real missing-data list; and read the whole history of a person on the record it describes. Missions 6 and 7 then add their stages — recruit doors and funnel, onboarding and consent — to these surfaces rather than inventing their own.
why_now: Nothing downstream can be specified until this exists: Missions 6 and 7 both write to the durable person record, both call the duplicate check, and both display their stages on the People and Roster surfaces. The gap is live rather than theoretical — on 2026-08-21 Brian created person records against the deployed application while testing operator invitations and could neither correct nor remove them (LAN-147); there is no person surface, no update operation anywhere in the service layer, and the only correction path today is hand-written SQL, which the working agreement reserves to Brian and forbids to every agent. A shipped decision is also due to be superseded: the vertical slice let any linked operator read contact values as an interim ruling, and Task 08 §6's four-role matrix supersedes it when this mission ships.
non_goals: No recruitment doors, funnel stages or recruit-stage fields; Mission 6 owns them, and nothing about the recruit process renders on a person record
No onboarding behaviour, collection requests or per-fact refused state; Mission 7 owns the chase, and this mission defines the queue it consumes
No consent capture, lawful basis, erasure or subject-access export; Missions 7 and 8
No season creation, opening, closing or rollover, and no season picker anywhere; Mission 11
No club-role or login grants; Administration and Roles already exist and are Mission 1's
No import of any kind; this mission closes walkable against seeded data only, and the season bootstrap and import moved to Mission 7 on 2026-08-26
No message composed, scheduled or sent, and no channel action beyond the voice call Task 08 §5 permits
No football semantics; Mission 9 owns what positions, jersey and coach group mean, and this mission gives them somewhere to live
No real member data in any environment, and no hosted migration
No Mission Lead work packages, worker assignment or implementation sequencing in this packet
No execution before Brian merges a ready packet version

sources.version: Portfolio v2 approved by Brian Schuster 2026-08-26; fetched 2026-08-26T13:41Z

requirements.text: A durable Person record carrying the thirteen approved person facts: first name, last name, aliases with one flagged as the display name, college email, personal email, mobile phone, college, matriculation year, expected graduation, degree field, date of birth, and a five-field emergency contact. Known-as is struck and collapses into alias, dropping the shipped known_as column.

One status the operator sees, assembled from two records: Recruit from the prospect record, then Onboarding, Active, Inactive, Departed and Archived from the membership. Five stored membership values; carried_forward, confirmed and withdrawn are struck. This supersedes OD-3 and is a frozen-model vocabulary change requiring a new enum type and a data migration that drops and recreates twelve dependent views.
The ladder is called Status on every surface. Standing was never an approved term and collided with alumni standing on the same record; renamed 2026-08-27.

Required-ness depends on where the person stands. Recruit: first name, last name, mobile. Coach, committee member or alumnus: those plus personal email. Onboarding, active or inactive player: those plus college, matriculation year, expected graduation, degree field, date of birth and emergency contact. Last name is required at every rung, amended 2026-08-27; roughly a quarter of the club will flag for it, which is the intent.

Every phone and email is validated before a save is offered, per field, naming the rule. A number is valid if it parses with its country code; only a bare national number defaults to UK. Correct numbers must never be refused, and the negative cases are acceptance criteria in their own right.
Contact values supersede rather than overwrite, preserving dated history and one preferred value per kind. Every other field overwrites, and its previous value survives in the person's history.

There is no contested-value state. The record shows the current value and who set it, because nothing goes higher than the operator. This supersedes Task 08 §6's disputed-awaiting-verification rule and the matching invariant in the mission overview.

No value carries a verification mark. Nothing in this application verifies that somebody holds a mailbox: contact_points has no verified column, no confirm-by-link flow exists, and this mission sends nothing. A value carries who supplied it and nothing more.

Where the mobile number being replaced is on WhatsApp for the active season, the correction surface says so before the save and states that the group membership ends and a rejoin will be asked for. It never claims the new number is or is not on WhatsApp. On WhatsApp has no substrate on main; Mission 6 verifies and Mission 4 must not send into an unverified presence.

A duplicate check runs before any person is created, matching first name, last name, aliases, every email and every phone. Its result must be answered: this is them, this is somebody new, or stop. Merged-away records are never offered. Creating over an exact contact-point match requires a reason, and rejected candidates are audited.

The add-person surface creates people and nothing else: no role, no login, no membership. Roles are assigned at /operate/admin/roles. A person created here has no tie to any season and appears only outside it until a role or a membership gives them one.

A merge preserves both identities and never deletes the losing row, which is marked merged and points at the survivor. The comparison is field by field with every difference marked; a reason is required; what will move is shown before it moves; there is no undo. An active operator seat on the losing record, and two memberships in one season, both refuse the merge. Duplicate prospect rows combine onto the survivor with the earliest first-contact date and the furthest-along status.

The roster is a board of eighteen columns in three labelled, tinted groups — Person, Onboarding, Season — wide, scrolling sideways inside its own container, with the player column pinned. Season facts edit in the cell: one click opens the value, a dropdown appears only where the value set is fixed, the change commits on its own, and every commit writes an audit event without asking for a reason. Person facts render and open the person record instead.

This mission builds the storage for the columns that have none: positions, jersey, coach group, formalwear, Blues, eligibility and availability. Mission 9 still owns what the football fields mean. Jersey is two columns — Blue # and White # — and the model is provisional: two kits, several numbers per player in one kit for about 8%, and numbers that are not unique.

Filtering is three things: a pinned set of Status, Availability and Missing onboarding data; a filter control in every other column header; and a Filtered by bar carrying every active filter as a removable chip with Clear all. A pinned control and its column header are one filter with two controls, each reflecting the other. Saved views are deferred.

Player detail carries the same Person, Onboarding and Season banding as the board, edits season facts in place with the same interaction, renders person facts and routes them to the person record, and retires the per-item Resolve/SAVE pair. The separate Membership status card folds into the Status field, taking the shipped activation control with it.

The missing-data queue lists every person with at least one required fact absent, naming which facts per row rather than a count, and never displaying a value. It filters by which fact is missing and by where the person stands. Its rows open the record and the correction. It is reached from a linked count on the roster and the People list, and from a Missing data entry in Administration.

Per-person history is a section of the person record, not a route. The What changed panel expands in place to every recorded change with its field and actor filters. A merge reads as one event naming what it moved; a superseded contact point reads as kept-and-dated. Player detail links rather than duplicating. W8 was struck from the frozen inventory on 2026-08-27 and absorbed here.

Every surface in this mission is four-role only — President, Vice-President, Secretary, General Manager. Anything the viewer's role does not grant is absent from the DOM and the payload, not hidden in it. Column visibility is a function of category grants, so widening access later drops restricted columns automatically.

Date of birth and emergency contact never appear on any list, board or queue. Emergency contact is third-party personal data and is locked down structurally: never a Person row, never a contact point, never reachable by any audience or messaging machinery, and out of leadership exports by default. Raw email and phone leave the roster grid, replaced by contactability indicators.

not recorded is explicit, visible and never defaulted, and never conflated with No — the lesson of the 2023 workbook's defaulting Rookie column. A derived value that cannot be derived says so rather than answering.
No surface carries narrative or explanatory prose. Labels, values and states, plus the single sentence an empty, refusal or error state genuinely needs.

Every edit is attributable and audited — actor, timestamp, field, before, after, and the reason where one was required. A reason is required to change an existing person value and never to fill an empty one. Cell edits on the board and on player detail write audit events and ask for no reason.

Every route this mission's workflows claim exists on the screen that claims it: Add a person and the linked missing count on the People list, Assign a role on the person record, the Missing data entry in Administration, and the person record's own history section. Five amendments against the approved W1 were raised by a sweep on 2026-08-27 and all are applied.

repository_drift.startup_rule: The Mission Lead compares current main to the baseline and runs the canonical harness drift checks before planning or dispatch. A newer main is acceptable only when this packet's meaning, feasibility, invariants, interfaces and acceptance are unchanged by it.
repository_drift.stop_rule: Stop and raise a packet revision when main has changed /operate/roster or /operate/roster/[membershipId], when membership_status or contact_points has moved under this mission, or when any surface this packet locks has been altered by another mission. W5 and W6 are photographed surfaces: a change to either must be re-photographed before the affected packages are dispatched, not merely re-read.
known_drift: Mission 4 (LAN-169 to LAN-173) executed during this intake. Its surface is messaging and scheduling, which this mission does not touch; inspected and confirmed harmless.
#94 gates implementation packages against their approved mockups at merge time (ADR 0037). It constrains execution rather than intake, and this mission produces the mockups it will be gated against.

main moved to be4f53d (#95 LAN-173, #97 LAN-178) after this packet was assembled and was merged in. Inspected: #95 added the follow-ups chase service and its own teardown fix for person_access_tokens; #97 bounds the Mission Lead to one derived epoch. Neither touches /operate/roster or /operate/roster/[membershipId], so W5 and W6's photographs stand and need no re-shoot.
